speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; to help you, I need to ask about your symptoms. How long have you had these symptoms, and have you noticed any fever, blood in your stool, or severe abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, combined with the onset of frequent watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, this presentation is highly suggestive of C. diff colitis. I am ready to confirm this with a stool toxin assay or C. diff PCR test.
